Perioperative Challenges of Unrepaired Tetralogy of Fallot in a Child With Severe Secondary Erythrocytosis: Lessons for the Modern Era.
items.abstract: In the United States, secondary erythrocytosis in children with unrepaired Tetralogy of Fallot (ToF) is rare yet may present in children from underresourced environments. We report our experience caring for a 5-year-old male with unrepaired ToF from a low-resourced country presenting with a hematocrit of 76.2%, requiring unique perioperative considerations. This work aligns with the unifying mission among congenital heart providers to improve access to high-quality surgery globally through collaboration.

items.title: Validation of the "Pathobiological Determinants of Atherosclerosis in Youth Risk Score" in a Norwegian Cohort of Young Adults.
Plasma Lipidome Is Dysregulated in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and Associated With Life-Course Adiposity Polygenic Risk.
items.abstract: Although both pre-symptomatic adiposity and dysregulated lipid metabolism are implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), the mechanistic pathways linking adiposity to disease remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate how genetic predisposition to adiposity might influence ALS through specific lipid metabolic pathways. We conducted mass spectrometry-based quantitative lipidomics on plasma from 104 ALS patients and 78 age- and sex-matched controls. Life-course adiposity polygenic risk scores (PRS) for birth weight, body fat percentage, appendicular lean mass and whole-body fat-free mass were constructed. Associations and PRS-by-disease interaction effects on the lipidome were evaluated. Compared to controls, ALS patients exhibited widespread lipid dysregulation. Seventy-eight lipid species were significantly altered (FDR    1.0), characterized by a predominant decrease in acylcarnitines (75% of species) and distinct shifts within sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid subclasses. A three-acylcarnitine candidate panel (C10:0, C12:0 and C18:2) using fivefold analysis with feature selection repeated within each training fold yielded an overall out-of-fold AUC of 0.958. Exploratory PRS-by-disease-status analyses identified 16 nominal interaction signals, including 13 acylcarnitines; no significant mediation effect of lipids between PRS and ALS risk was detected. These findings identify robust ALS-associated plasma lipid alterations, and our exploratory findings suggest that genetic predisposition to adiposity may shape the pattern of lipid metabolic disruption in ALS, offering new insights into the disease's metabolic pathophysiology.

items.title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T and I Discordance in Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors.
items.abstract: Serial troponin monitoring is used during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but guidelines do not specify whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) or T (hs-cTnT) should be measured. Unlike cardiac-specific hs-cTnI, hs-cTnT can rise from noncardiac sources. This study sought to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of hs-cTnT/hs-cTnI discordance, identify clinical correlates, and evaluate prognostic implications in ambulatory ICI-treated patients. In this prospective single-center cohort, patients starting ICI therapy underwent paired hs-cTnT (Roche Elecsys) and hs-cTnI (Siemens Atellica) measurements in the same banked samples at baseline and 1 month. Patients with adjudicated ICI-associated myocarditis or myositis were excluded by design. Among 433 patients with paired baseline measurements, hs-cTnT was elevated in 37.9% and hs-cTnI in 1.8%; 158 (36.5%) were discordant (elevated hs-cTnT, normal hs-cTnI), and 267 (61.7%) had normal levels of both (κ = 0.036). Among 329 patients with paired data at baseline and 1 month, discordance prevalence was unchanged (38.3% vs 38.0%; McNemar P > 0.99). Independent correlates were older age, male sex, and chronic kidney disease (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 30.1 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier), elevated hs-cTnT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.00-1.81; P = 0.048); only 8 of 231 deaths (3.5%) were cardiac. In ambulatory patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy, over one-third had elevated hs-cTnT with normal hs-cTnI: a stable, nonspecific pattern present before ICI exposure and consistent with noncardiac sources rather than acute cardiac injury. hs-cTnI is the more cardiac-specific assay; paired baseline measurement of both troponins may help contextualize later elevations when myocarditis is suspected.

items.title: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of Statin-Naïve Anti-HMGCR Myopathy: Case Series and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-associated myopathy is a rare form of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy most commonly reported in patients exposed to statins. However, its occurrence in statin-naïve individuals is increasingly recognized but remains underreported. We describe two unusual cases of statin-naïve anti-HMGCR myopathy presenting with severe rhabdomyolysis, leading to acute kidney injury in one patient and dropped head syndrome in another, emphasizing that anti-HMGCR IMNM should be suspected even in statin-naïve individuals presenting with unexplained myopathy, rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI, or axial muscle weakness such as dropped head syndrome, as early immunotherapy may significantly improve outcomes.

items.title: Immune Evasion by CMV and BK Virus: Lurking Viruses Waiting for the Right Moment to Deliver a Fatal Blow to Individuals With Compromised Immunity.
items.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (CMV) and BK polyomavirus are archetypal latent DNA viruses that establish lifelong persistence and cause severe disease upon reactivation in immunocompromised hosts. Although they differ markedly in virion architecture, genome size, and coding capacity, both viruses converge on a shared biological principle: durable persistence is achieved through sustained immune invisibility rather than maximal replication. CMV is a large, enveloped double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) virus whose multilayered structure supports the expression of numerous immunomodulatory proteins that disrupt antigen processing and presentation, modulate natural killer cell surveillance, and reshape cytokine and chemokine networks. In contrast, BK virus (BKV) is a small, nonenveloped dsDNA virus that achieves immune evasion through functional minimalism, restricting viral gene expression, limiting antigen availability, and attenuating innate immune sensing pathways. These distinct yet convergent immune evasion strategies complicate diagnosis, constrain the efficacy of antiviral therapies, and promote viral persistence in vulnerable patients. By integrating structural and biological features with mechanisms of immune escape, this review primarily focuses on how immune modulation blurs the classical distinction between latency and active infection, highlighting implications for clinical monitoring, therapy, and emerging immune-guided strategies for the effective control of viral infection in immunocompromised individuals.

items.title: Evaluating a multi-vaccine respiratory immunization strategy involving SARS-CoV-2, pneumococcal, and influenza vaccines in adults: A randomized, open-label, multicenter, controlled, non-inferiority Phase IV trial in China.
items.abstract: Co-administration of vaccines targeting multiple respiratory pathogens may enhance coverage and streamline adult immunization programs. We conducted a randomized, multicentre, open-label Phase IV trial registered at Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100046227) in China to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of co-administering an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (WIBP-CorV) with the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPV23) and a quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV4). A total of 1,404 adults aged ≥ 18 year, including equal numbers of adults aged 18-59 year and ≥60 year, were randomized 1:1:1 to receive WIBP-CorV + PPV23 on Day 0 followed by WIBP-CorV + IIV4 on Day 28, WIBP-CorV alone on Days 0 and 28, or PPV23 on Day 0 followed by IIV4 on Day 28. Co-administration preserved humoral immune responses across vaccine platforms. Non-inferiority in geometric mean titers or concentrations was demonstrated for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pneumococcal serotype-specific IgG responses. Seroconversion rates were non-inferior to those following separate administration for all pneumococcal serotypes, though results were less consistent for SARS-CoV-2 (after the second dose) and influenza A(H1N1). Age-stratified analyses showed age- and strain-specific non-inferiority findings that should be interpreted cautiously. Co-administration demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, with only slightly higher rates of mild, transient local reactions and no vaccine-related serious adverse events (SAEs). These findings support the feasibility of co-administering WIBP-CorV with PPV23 and IIV4 while maintaining immunogenicity and safety in adults represented in this study. Trial registration The study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) under registration number ChiCTR2100046227. A Phase IV trial evaluated co-administration of COVID-19, PPV23 and IIV4.Co-administration preserved immunogenicity across multiple vaccine platforms.Non-inferiority was achieved for most predefined immunogenicity endpoints.No vaccine-related serious adverse events were observed.Findings support integrated adult respiratory vaccination strategies.

A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
items.abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

items.title: Exploratory associations of gut microbiota composition with HBeAg and HBsAg status in nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: HBeAg and HBsAg reflect viral replication and host immune status and are important determinants of treatment responsiveness in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The gut microbiota, a key component of the gut-liver axis, may influence immune regulation and antiviral outcomes. This study characterized gut microbiota profiles across different HBeAg and HBsAg statuses in CHB patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. Fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 29 healthy controls (HC) and 101 NA-treated CHB patients without cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, including 30 HBeAg-positive (EP) and 71 HBeAg-negative (EN) individuals. The EN group was further stratified by serum HBsAg levels into an advantageous subgroup ( n = 57) and a non-advantageous subgroup (≥1,500 IU/mL, n = 14). Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly among EP, EN, and HC groups. Species-level analyses identified nominal group-related differences in several Bacteroidales- and Firmicutes-associated anaerobic commensals, including Bacteroides uniformis, Blautia obeum, Eubacterium ventriosum, Anaerobutyricum, and Parabacteroides timonensis; however, none remained significant after global FDR correction across all detected species. Within the EN group, selected taxa showed directionally consistent associations with HBsAg strata in downsampling, leave-one-out, and CLR-based sensitivity analyses, but these subgroup findings also did not remain significant after FDR correction. NA-treated CHB was associated with exploratory taxonomic differences without detectable loss of microbial diversity. The observed associations with HBeAg status and HBsAg burden were hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger longitudinal cohorts incorporating absolute microbial quantification, targeted metabolomics, host immune profiling, and more complete dietary, anthropometric, and other relevant clinical covariates.

items.title: The aMAP Score Effectively Stratifies Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk in the Steatotic Liver Disease Population.
items.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is an increasingly important cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet validated risk stratification tools remain limited. We aim to evaluate the aMAP score, initially developed for HCC risk prediction mainly in viral hepatitis across international cohorts, in the SLD population. 156 406 SLD participants were included from the UK Biobank (UKB) and 3166 SLD patients with virally suppressed chronic hepatitis B from a Chinese cohort. The predictive and stratification performance of the aMAP score was assessed and compared with the PAGE-B, mPAGE-B, CAMD and MASLD-HCC scores. A refined stratification of the aMAP-defined high-risk population identified a subgroup exceeding the recommended surveillance threshold. Median follow-up was 13.64 years in UKB and 9.97 years in the Chinese cohort, with 287 and 58 patients developing HCC, respectively. The aMAP score showed favourable discrimination (C-indices: 0.80 [95% CI, 0.78-0.83] in UKB; 0.79 [95% CI, 0.73-0.85] in the Chinese cohort). The 15-year cumulative HCC incidence by aMAP in UKB was 0.06% (95% CI, 0.04%-0.08%), 0.26% (95% CI, 0.21%-0.31%) and 1.43% (95% CI, 1.14%-1.72%) for low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups (high vs. low risk, sHR: 28.51; 95% CI, 19.58-41.52; Gray's test p   64) identified a very-high-risk subgroup in UKB with 15-year cumulative incidences of 3.08% (training; 95% CI, 1.29%-4.87%) and 5.35% (validation; 95% CI, 3.04%-7.67%). The aMAP score is an effective tool for HCC risk stratification among SLD patients. The refined aMAP threshold accurately identifies very-high-risk patients qualifying for guideline-recommended surveillance. Steatotic liver disease is an increasingly important cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet many cases occur before cirrhosis and validated risk stratification tools remain limited. In two large cohorts from the UK Biobank and China, the aMAP score effectively distinguished individuals with different risks of HCC. A higher aMAP cutoff further identified a very‐high‐risk group that reached the recommended threshold and warranted regular HCC surveillance.

items.title: HIV screening in patients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections in Spanish emergency departments.
items.abstract: To estimate the frequency of HIV serology requests in emergency departments (EDs) in Spain for patients with sexually transmitted infections (STIs), its longitudinal evolution (2018-2024), and associated factors. Multi-center study including all patients diagnosed with an STI across 14 EDs in 8 Spanish autonomous communities. Demographics, specific STI diagnoses, prior HIV testing, and HIV serology requested during ED care were recorded. Differences and temporal trends were analyzed. Among 35,845 STI cases (median age 34 years; 60% men; 74% Spanish; 2% previously tested for HIV), HIV serology was requested in 5,462 (15%), yielding 253 (4.6%) positive results. Main diagnoses included orchiepididymitis (24.9%), vulvovaginitis (16.4%), and non-specific urethritis (12.4%). HIV testing increased significantly from 5.3% in 2018 to 20.7% in 2024 (p < 0.001). Higher testing likelihood was associated with younger age (aOR 0.97 per year, 95% CI 0.97-0.97), male sex (aOR 3.83, 95% CI 3.35-4.37), prior HIV testing (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 1.08-1.92), and more recent years (aOR 1.34 per year, 95% CI 1.30-1.38). Testing rates varied significantly by specific STI, with higher probabilities in risk exposure, suspected STI, and urethritis but lower probabilities in orchiepididymitis, vulvovaginitis, and genital herpes. HIV screening among patients presenting with STIs in Spanish EDs remains low (15%), despite a significant upward trend over time. Disparities based on age, sex, and specific STI presentation highlight the need for universal HIV screening protocols across all ED patients diagnosed with an STI. Estimar la frecuencia de solicitud de serología de VIH en urgencias hospitalarias en España en pacientes con infecciones de transmisión sexual (ITS), su evolución temporal (2018–2024) y sus factores asociados. Estudio multicéntrico que incluyó a todos los pacientes diagnosticados de ITS en 14 servicios de urgencias de 8 comunidades autónomas. Se registraron variables demográficas, diagnósticos específicos de ITS, cribados previos de VIH y serologías de VIH solicitadas durante la atención en urgencias. Se analizaron las diferencias y las tendencias temporales. De 35.845 casos de ITS (mediana de edad 34 años; 60% varones; 74% españoles; 2% con cribado previo de VIH), se solicitó serología de VIH en 5.462 (15%), resultando positivas 253 (4,6%). Los diagnósticos más frecuentes fueron orquiepididimitis (24,9%), vulvovaginitis (16,4%) y uretritis no específica (12,4%). La realización de pruebas de VIH aumentó significativamente del 5,3% en 2018 al 20,7% en 2024 (p<0,001). Una mayor probabilidad de cribado se asoció con menor edad (ORa 0,97 por año, IC 95% 0,97–0,97), sexo masculino (ORa 3,83, IC 95% 3,35–4,37), cribado previo de VIH (ORa 1,44, IC 95% 1,08–1,92) y años más recientes (ORa 1,34 por año, IC 95% 1,30–1,38). Las tasas de cribado variaron según la ITS, con mayor probabilidad en exposición de riesgo, sospecha de ITS y uretritis, y menor en orquiepididimitis, vulvovaginitis y herpes genital. El cribado de VIH en pacientes con ITS en urgencias sigue siendo bajo (15%), a pesar de una tendencia ascendente significativa. Las disparidades según edad, sexo y diagnóstico de ITS subrayan la necesidad de implementar protocolos de cribado universal en todos los pacientes diagnosticados de ITS en urgencias.

items.title: Current progress in the pathophysiology and potential therapeutic targets of acute-on-chronic liver failure through multiomics approaches.
items.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a severe clinical syndrome that develops in patients with chronic hepatitis or liver cirrhosis. It is characterized by a high mortality rate, rapid progression, and complex pathological mechanisms. As it often involves multiorgan failure (e.g., of the liver, kidneys, and brain), traditional clinical indicators have limited predictive value and cannot support accurate, personalized treatment. However, the rapid development of omics sequencing technologies in recent years (e.g., genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics) has provided unprecedented opportunities to analyze the molecular mechanisms of ACLF, discover novel biomarkers, and develop precise intervention strategies. Multiomics technology is an approach that systematically studies complex biological mechanisms of ACLF by integrating data from multiple omics disciplines. This approach overcomes the limitations of single-omics techniques, and offering a more comprehensive view of disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, and precision medicine. In this review, we summarize studies on whole-genome sequencing, single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, proteomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics in patients with ACLF and discuss associations between expression patterns, disease progression and prognosis, and the interconnections among multiomics.

items.title: Integrative computational simulations uncover the conformational activation pathway of AKT1 kinase.
items.abstract: The AKT1 kinase, a central node in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling axis, governs critical cellular processes, including survival and proliferation, and its dysregulation drives cancer, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. While structural studies have resolved static snapshots of AKT1's inactive and active states, the dynamic mechanisms orchestrating its activation, particularly the coupling of phosphorylation-induced signals to catalytic competency, remain poorly resolved. This knowledge gap hinders the development of targeted therapies addressing AKT1's pathological hyperactivation. Using integrative computational approaches, we characterize the hierarchical conformational transitions enabling AKT1 activation at atomic resolution. Microsecond-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and nudged elastic band (NEB) pathway analyses reveal that phosphorylation at T308 initiates a metastable "pre-active" state, destabilizing autoinhibitory interactions at the PH-kinase interface. This triggers potential structural rearrangements: (1) A-loop opening exposes the hydrophobic motif for regulatory phosphorylation, (2) αC-helix rotation establishes the Lys179-Glu198 catalytic salt bridge, and (3) DFG motif flipping enables Asp292-Mg 2+ coordination, completing the active site assembly. By mapping the energy landscape of AKT1 activation, this work bridges static structural data with dynamic mechanistic insights, offering a framework for therapeutic intervention against AKT1-driven pathologies.

items.title: Tiny Travelers, Big Impact: Physiological Effects of Extracellular Vesicles on the Blood-Brain Barrier.
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier [BBB] is a highly specialized structure that regulates the influx and efflux of nutrients and metabolic waste to maintain homeostasis of the central nervous system. This selective permeability of the BBB is sustained by tight junctions that are supported by pericytes and astrocytes. Recently, extracellular vesicles have emerged as mediators of intercellular communication across and within the BBB. This review examines the bidirectional transport of EVs across the BBB and the distinct functional impacts of blood-borne EVs. On the luminal side, circulating EVs derived from platelets, erythrocytes, and leukocytes convey systemic signals to the neurovasculature. Platelet-derived EVs deliver growth factors and lipid mediators that promote vascular repair and modulate adaptive immunity during endothelial disruption. Erythrocyte-derived EVs selectively shed surface markers like CD47 to regulate cellular turnover while simultaneously providing phosphatidylserine that maintains hemostasis and nitric oxide bioavailability. Meanwhile, leukocytic-derived EVs protect and transport immunological cargo, such as MHC complexes and cytokines, functioning as critical sensors and amplifiers of immune surveillance at the vascular interface. Together, these circulating EV populations influence endothelial signaling, transporter expression, and tight junction integrity from the vascular side. Conversely, on the abluminal side, the roles of brain parenchymal-derived EVs secreted by astrocytes, pericytes, neurons, and microglia are explored in regulating local neurovascular coupling, vascular tone, and endothelial responsiveness. Within this microenvironment, astrocyte-derived EVs provide neurotrophic and neuroprotective support by delivering angiogenic factors and cytoprotective chaperone proteins like HSP70 to protect cells from mechanical and oxidative stress. Pericyte-derived EVs preserve microvascular barrier integrity by transporting regulatory microRNAs and angiopoietin-1 to directly upregulate endothelial tight junction proteins. Furthermore, neuron-derived EVs participate in activity-dependent signaling, transferring vital microRNAs to endothelial cells to promote vascular stability and support synaptic plasticity. By framing the BBB as an active communication system, this review underscores how peripheral and central EVs integrate systemic and neural environments, highlighting their fundamental roles in BBB physiology and, beyond, their profound implications as biomarkers of CNS distress and programmable vehicles for targeted drug delivery.

items.title: Developing a Better Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treatment: AlEu MOF Nanoparticles Enhance Microwave Thermal Ablation and Synergistically Activate the cGAS-STING Pathway.
items.abstract: To address the high recurrence rate of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following microwave ablation (MWA) therapy, this study develops aluminum-europium metal-organic framework (AlEu MOF) nanoparticles that enhance MWA efficacy by physically improving thermal ablation and activating cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING)-mediated antitumor immunity. AlEu MOF nanoparticles were synthesized via a one-pot hydrothermal method and characterized for physicochemical properties. Biocompatibility and in vitro cell-killing efficacy in combination with MWA were evaluated in Hepa1-6 cell lines. Immunostimulatory capacity was assessed by measuring activation markers of the cGAS-STING pathway. In vivo antitumor efficacy was investigated in a Hepa1-6 subcutaneous tumor-bearing mouse model, with monitoring of tumor growth, intratumoral temperature elevation, serum levels of cGAS-STING pathway downstream effectors, and treatment safety. AlEu MOF nanoparticles demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and hemocompatibility. In combination with MWA, AlEu MOF significantly enhanced thermal efficiency within tumors, resulting in superior tumor growth inhibition compared with MWA alone. Mechanistically, the enhanced thermal ablation triggered mitochondrial damage and downstream cGAS-STING pathway activation, as evidenced by elevated serum levels of key downstream cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-6 and TNF-α) in the combination therapy group. No significant hepatorenal toxicity or major organ damage was observed throughout the treatment period. The AlEu MOF nanoparticles potentiate MWA therapy through a dual synergistic mechanism: enhanced thermal ablation serves as the upstream trigger for cGAS-STING activation, while europium ions simultaneously amplify the STING signaling output, together converting local thermal ablation into systemic antitumor immunity. This synergistic strategy offers a promising approach for enhancing both local tumor ablation and systemic antitumor immunity in HCC.

items.title: Network analysis of core symptom changes in hepatocellular carcinoma survivors after transarterial chemoembolization: A longitudinal study.
items.abstract: The aims of this study were to explore the longitudinal trajectories of core symptoms in survivors with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and to analyze their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and unmet supportive care needs. This longitudinal study enrolled 271 HCC survivors undergoing TACE in China. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at three time points-24 h (T1), 7 days (T2), and 1 month (T3) post-TACE-using four validated instruments: the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory-Chinese Version (MDASI-C), the Tumor Symptom Measure for Primary Liver Cancer (TSM-PLC), the Quality of Life Instrument for Liver Cancer (QOL-LC V2.0), and the Short Form of Survivors' Unmet Needs Scale (SF-SUNS). Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to extract discrete symptom clusters, and network analysis was used to calculate strength centrality (rs)-an index quantifying the sum of absolute edge weights connecting each symptom to all others-to identify core symptoms. Five symptom clusters were identified at T1: Fatigue-Cognitive, Post-embolization, Somatic, Emotional, and Hepatobiliary-Specific. The Post-embolization cluster was present only at T1, whereas the remaining four clusters persisted at T2 and T3. However, the core symptom shifted over time: nausea at T1 (rs = 1.154), lack of appetite at T2 (rs = 1.229), and sadness at T3 (rs = 1.107). HRQoL was lowest at T1, improved at T2, and declined at T3, with all pairwise comparisons significant (all p p p < 0.01). During the first month post-TACE, the sequence of core symptoms transitioned from nausea to lack of appetite and then to sadness, suggesting time-specific supportive care strategies-including antiemetic prophylaxis, nutritional support, and psychosocial care. Routine assessment of unmet needs may help reduce symptom burden and optimize long-term HRQoL for these survivors.
